title: Office front page — round 2: your notes applied

steps.headline: "Open a file…" is now "Browse files" with a folder icon, and the search box sits to its right.
steps.changed: Your R-1 note: button renamed and given a folder icon; search moved to the far right of the Recent line.
steps.notice: The button still opens your computer's file picker, Office files only.

steps.path: Office → Home → point at any file
steps.headline: The four buttons now sit fully right, in the place of "Opened … ago", which fades out as they fade in.
steps.changed: Your R-2 note: the time and the buttons share one spot at the right edge, so nothing in the row shifts. The buttons also slide in a few pixels as they appear (a fifth of a second).
steps.notice: The time comes back as soon as the pointer leaves the row.
steps.risk: On a touch screen there is no pointing, so the buttons stay and the time is hidden there. With your computer's reduce-motion setting on, the swap happens without the slide.

steps.headline: Rename now opens a small popup like Rename session: the name, Save, Cancel — no box inside the row.
steps.changed: Your R-2/R-4 notes: the in-row box is gone. The popup is the same shape as renaming a session, with the name picked out ready to type over.
steps.notice: The ending (.docx) isn't in the box, and the line under it says it stays, so the file keeps opening in Office. A taken name shows its reason at the top of the popup and keeps what you typed.

steps.path: Office → Home (live, in the test app)
steps.headline: Try it: point at a few files, right-click one, rename one — does the fade feel right?
steps.hint: This is the real page against pretend files. Point at rows to see the fade; Rename, Make a copy and Remove from Recent work here but touch no real files.
steps.notice: Watch the time fade out and the buttons slide in as you move down the list.
